## PART 2. WHAT HAPPENED, IN ORDER

Each item is one fact, with its source page. Items are numbered F1 to F41 and are referred to by number in Parts 3 to 6, so nothing is said twice.

### Stage one: the defendants were the owners' tenants (1975 to 2016)

F1. The defendants' own verified Answer admits that the family occupied the 2,587-square-meter portion from 1975 as renters of the owners' administrator. "They paid monthly rent to the previous administrator Ben Llamanzares through Manuel Violeta" (paragraph 40); "from 1975 while they were renting the property, to the time that it was offered for them to purchase" (paragraph 43); "they regularly paid rent to the previous administrator" (paragraph 44[b]). These are judicial admissions under Rule 129, Section 4. They need no proof. [Annex A, pp. 3, 4] [IN EVIDENCE]

F2. All three defense witnesses swear the same. Salvador dela Fuente: the Balanes agreed to buy "ang lupain na kanilang nirerentahan" (the land they were renting) and he collected "mga bayad sa upa" (rent payments). Princess Balane Torralba: "noong una ay nirerentahan lang ito ng aking magulang" (at first my parents only rented it). Engr. Erwin Balane: "noong una, umuupa lamang ang aming pamilya sa property na iyon" (at first our family only rented that property). [Annex Q, pp. 2, 4 (Salvador); pp. 5, 7 (Princess); pp. 8, 9 (Erwin)] [IN EVIDENCE when affirmed]

F3. The owners' written authority to Cesar is the Special Power of Attorney of 16 March 1992, executed in Los Angeles by Geraldine K. Hoppe, Patricia K. Zschoche and Marcia Ellen Keesey. Paragraph 6 states its purpose: to settle unpaid real estate taxes by negotiating a sale "to interested third parties." Paragraph 7 then confines the sale to a class and a condition. Cesar is appointed "to negotiate for the sale of the above-described real estate property in favor of third persons in possession of CONTRACTS TO SELL executed by the previous administrator, MR. BEN LLAMANZARES and/or to those who have paid their downpayments or have made partial payments therefor to the latter. Said sale shall be upon such terms and conditions and under such covenants which said Attorney-in-Fact may deem fit, proper and convenient, after prior consultation with us, and to sign and execute the necessary documents, agreements and other legal papers pertaining thereto as well as to receive the proceeds of the aforementioned sale in our collective behalf." The words "in possession" govern "CONTRACTS TO SELL," not the land. The class is holders of a Llamanzares contract to sell, or persons who had paid Llamanzares a down payment or partial payment. Every sale required prior consultation with the owners. The property the SPA describes is the mother parcel: "covered by Transfer Certificate of Title No. T-4497 ... Lot 2 of the subdivision plan (LRC) Psd-12802 ... ONE HUNDRED THIRTY NINE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED THIRTY TWO SQUARE METERS (139,132)," held by the three sisters as "undivided interests" after their 1988 extrajudicial settlement (paragraphs 1 to 3). It names no derivative title and no lot of T-52540. [Annex B, pp. 2, 3 (paragraphs 1 to 9)] [IN EVIDENCE: plaintiff's Exh. E; defense Exh. 7]

F4. That SPA was annotated on TCT No. T-52540 on 21 June 1996. The entry reads "appointing CESAR M. DELA FUENTE, as atty-in-fact of GERALDINE K. HOPPE ET AL., to sign, negotiate for the sale of the parcel of land in this title." This is the defendants' best fact, and it is also ours: from 1996 the registry itself sent every buyer to the instrument, and the instrument contains the class limit and the consultation clause (PD 1529, Section 52). Complaint paragraph 50 says the SPA was annotated only in 2021. That is wrong and must be corrected before the defense uses it. [Annex C, p. 2] [IN EVIDENCE: Exh. B]

F5. No defendant was ever in the class. The defendants plead a 1980s down payment of Three Thousand Pesos (P3,000.00) to Llamanzares through Violeta (Answer paragraph 40). There is no receipt for it. The earliest receipt in their Exhibit 5 is dated October 2[5], 2003 [VERIFY day], from Efren Balane, One Thousand Pesos (P1,000.00), "as payment for lot in Mercedes." The only receipt that says "Down payment" is dated 6 January 2005, Twenty Thousand Pesos (P20,000.00), signed "Von dela Fuente," that is, Salvador. Both are payments to Cesar's side, not to Llamanzares. Neither is a contract to sell. [Annex D, pp. 2, 3; Annex A, p. 3] [IN EVIDENCE: defense Exh. 5]

F6. On 15 August 2005 the three owners revoked Cesar's authority. The instrument, acknowledged the same day before Vice Consul Noemi T. Diaz in Los Angeles, appoints a different attorney-in-fact and ends: "Any Special Power of Attorney in favor of any person other than [the new attorney-in-fact] is hereby disowned and should be deemed without force and effect." The revocation was never annotated on T-52540. [Annex H, pp. 1, 2] [IN EVIDENCE: Exh. F]

F7. On 29 December 2006, after the revocation, Princess Balane paid Three Thousand Pesos (P3,000.00) to Villafuerte Engineering and Surveying Office for a "subdivision survey of lot owned by the H[ei]rs of Worrick Keesey segregating a portion thereof in favor of the above-named." The receipt is in the defendants' own Exhibit 5. In 2006 the family paid to survey land it was told, in writing, belonged to the Keesey heirs. [Annex D, p. 1] [IN EVIDENCE]

F8. From March 2007 to September 2014 the family paid on printed receipts of the "HEIRS OF MARY W. KEESEY ESTATE," each with an "Occupant's Name" line and a "Payment for the month of" line. Fifteen receipts bill a named month: March, April, May, June and July 2007 (payor Princess Balane, One Thousand to Two Thousand Pesos each); September 2013 to September 2014 (payor "Golly Balane" or "Mrs. Golly Balane," Two Thousand Pesos each). A monthly bill in the name of an "Occupant" is rent. The defendants offered this series "to prove rents paid" (Answer paragraph 61[e]). [Annex D, pp. 9, 10, 11, 22 to 26; Annex A, p. 8] [IN EVIDENCE]

F9. Princess Balane Torralba, now a Municipal Councilor, was the named payor on about forty-five receipts from 2007 to 2012 [VERIFY count], including a Fifteen Thousand Peso (P15,000.00) "partial payment for lot" [VERIFY year]. Her judicial affidavit swears she had no part in the sale "maliban na lang sa tumulong ako sa gastusin sa pagpa-survey" (except that I helped with the survey expense). [Annex D, pp. 9 to 12, 21; Annex Q, p. 6 (Princess)]

F10. Salvador dela Fuente swears the owners never personally dealt with Cesar after 1992 and that nobody consulted them: "Wala po. Hindi naman sila umuuwi sa Pilipinas. Ang madalas lang po na kausap ng aking ama ay ang Agcaoili law office sa Maynila" (No. They never came home to the Philippines. The one my father usually spoke to was the Agcaoili law office in Manila). The owners' Manila counsel was known and reachable. The consultation the SPA required was never sought. [Annex Q, p. 4 (Salvador)]

### Stage two: the deed, the lost-title petition and the re-papering (2016 to 2017)

F11. On 27 September 2016 Cesar swore before Atty. Elaine Gay R. Belen that the owner's duplicate of T-52540 was lost. Two days later, on 29 September 2016, he signed the Deed of Absolute Sale in favor of Gloria H. Balane before Atty. Donald E. Asis (Doc. No. 304, Page 61, Book CXVI, series of 2016) for Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P250,000.00), reciting the price as "to me in hand paid by and receipt whereof is hereby acknowledged." Gloria did not sign the deed; the two instrumental witnesses are unnamed. The loss affidavit was entered on the title on 10 October 2016, eleven days after the deed. [Annex E, p. 1; Annex C, p. 3] [IN EVIDENCE: Exh. H; defense Exh. 6; Exh. B]

F12. The price was not in hand on 29 September 2016. The defendants' own receipts continue after the deed: 30 September 2016, Sixty Thousand Pesos (P60,000.00); 7 October 2016, Ten Thousand; 18 November 2016, Forty Thousand (Receipt No. 0219, "Forty Thousand Pesos"); 27 November 2016, Twenty Thousand; 1 December 2016, Forty Thousand; December 2016, Thirty Thousand; 7 January 2017, Two Thousand; 30 January 2017, Three Thousand; and February 2017, Receipt No. 0228, "Full payment for lot in San Roque, Mercedes CN." The deed's receipt clause was false on the day it was signed, and the buyer accepted a deed from an agent who was still collecting. The serial numbers also run backwards against the dates (No. 0219 dated 18 November comes after No. 0222 dated 30 September; No. 0226 dated 30 January 2017 comes after No. 0227 dated 7 January 2017). [Annex D, pp. 29 to 32] [IN EVIDENCE]

F13. By a petition dated in October 2016 and filed on 20 October 2016, Cesar petitioned RTC Branch 41 (Special Proceeding No. 2156) for new owner's duplicates of seven titles, T-52540 included, describing himself as "Attorney-in-Fact, Representative and Administrator of the Estate of the late Marry Worrick Keesey," eleven years after his authority was revoked. He swore the titles had been "in a filing cabinet at his house." The petition does not mention that he had sold a portion of T-52540 three weeks earlier. Counsel was the same Atty. Belen who notarized the loss affidavit. [Annex F, pp. 1 to 4] [TO OFFER: certified copy requested]

F14. The authority annexed to that petition was not the 1992 SPA but a 1991 SPA (Makati, Atty. Agcaoili) that grants administration only: supervision, taxes, collections, deposits and representation before the BIR, the Registry and the DAR. It contains no power to sell. The Registry annotated this 1991 SPA on T-52540 under the same entry number and the same timestamp as the loss affidavit (Entry No. 2016002312, 10 October 2016, 01:43:44 PM), with the description "with power to sign." [Annex F, pp. 5, 6; Annex C, p. 3]

F15. Notice in the petition went to the Provincial Prosecutor and the Registry of Deeds, with posting on three bulletin boards. The pages in hand show no notice to the three registered owners. Page 2 of the November 2016 order, which would carry the notice directives, is missing from our copy. [Annex F, pp. 7, 8, 9, 10] [VERIFY against the certified record]

F16. Under oath in January 2017 Cesar told the court the registered owners knew of the case and were "making follow ups," that he was "authorized by the registered owner," that he himself would receive the new duplicates, and, asked who was in actual possession of the properties, answered "I." The Balanes were in possession of the portion he had just sold. [Annex F, pp. 12, 13, 14]

F17. The order of 30 January 2017 directed new duplicates for all seven titles, including TCT No. T-38838, a title cancelled in 1999. The certificate of finality issued 13 March 2017. The new duplicate of T-52540 was entered on 16 March 2017. [Annex F, pp. 15, 16, 17; Annex C, p. 3; Annex G, p. 3] [IN EVIDENCE: Exh. B-1 (entry only)]

F18. Within two days and fifteen days of the finality respectively, two instruments were notarized by Atty. Asis in the same Book CXXII: a Partition-Subdivision Agreement dated 15 March 2017 (Doc. No. 402, Page 81) and a Deed of Confirmation dated 28 March 2017 (Doc. No. 115, Page 23). The later-dated act sits two hundred eighty-seven entries and fifty-eight pages earlier in the same notarial book. One of the two dates is not the date of entry. [INFERRED; the notarial register decides this] [Annex C, p. 4; Annex G, p. 1]

F19. In the Deed of Confirmation, Cesar alone, as "authorized representative of the registered owners," confirms that the portion sold to Gloria is land "registered in the name of GERALDINE K. HOPPE, PATRICIA K. ZSCHOCHE & MARCIA ELLEN KESSEY." Gloria does not sign. No instrumental witness is identifiable. An agent cannot ratify his own unauthorized act for the principals. [Annex G, p. 1] [TO OFFER: RD CTC Ref. 2022006350 in hand]

F20. Cesar died on 21 June 2017. Everything that follows was done by others in his name. [TO OFFER: PSA death certificate]

### Stage three: knowledge before registration (2019 to 2021)

F21. On 15 August 2019 the owners' counsel, Agcaoili & Associates, wrote that Cesar's SPA "was revoked by the Keeseys on 15 August 2005" and that "any and all transactions entered into by the late Mr. De La Fuente after said date were unauthorized and, therefore, void." The letter is copied to "Atty. Elaine R. Belen, IBP Office, Hall of Justice Bldg., Daet." Proof that she received it is not in hand. [Annex J, p. 1] [TO OFFER; receipt to be proved]

F22. By 11 February 2020 Gloria had a lawyer writing on her behalf about this parcel. The Provincial Prosecutor's resolution on her sister's complaint records "a letter from their counsel, dated February 11, 2020, reminding the herein complainant ... to desist from making any construction." Who that lawyer was is not yet in hand. [Annex O, pp. 7, 8]

F23. On 28 May 2020, in Toronto, Gloria executed a Special Power of Attorney appointing her sister Nelly Juntilla "to institute or file action regarding property in Purok 4, Barangay San Roque, Mercedes ... and defend me from any action that may be filed in relation thereto." She described the property by the heirs' own tax declaration, ARP No. GR-2014-HH-07-001-00247, and as "Lot 2-X-6-I-4-C ... with an area of TWENTY ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED FORTY EIGHT (21,148) SQUARE METERS," which is the whole lot then titled to the three sisters, not her 2,587 square meters. Paragraph 5 withholds "any power to alienate, sell, transfer, mortgage or convey." She knew how a principal grants, and withholds, the power to sell. This SPA is Annex "1" to the defendants' Answer, and Juntilla verified the Answer under it. [Annex M, pp. 1 to 3; Annex A, p. 13] [IN EVIDENCE: defense annex]

F24. The tax declaration she cited, ARP No. 00247, is declared to "HRS. OF MARY WORRICK KEESEY NAMELY: GERALDINE K. HOPPE, PATRICIA K. ZSCHOCHE and MARCIA ELLEN KEESEY," address "#4814 ADELE COURT WOODLAND HILLS, CALIFORNIA, USA." In May 2020 Gloria held a document that named the owners and gave their address. [Annex M, p. 4] [TO OFFER: certified copy from the Municipal Assessor]

F25. In June 2020 the deed moved for the first time since 2016. Capital gains tax of Two Hundred Eighty-Seven Thousand Eight Hundred Sixty-Six Pesos and Seventy-Three Centavos (P287,866.73) and documentary stamp tax of Seventy-Seven Thousand Four Hundred Seventy-Eight Pesos and Eight Centavos (P77,478.08) were paid on 15 June 2020. The first eCAR, No. 201900074035 of 19 June 2020, was issued under TCT No. T-38838, the title cancelled in 1999, and Tax Declaration No. HH-07-001-00246. The Provincial Treasurer's certificate of 24 June 2020 shows transfer tax of Twelve Thousand Five Hundred Forty-Seven Pesos (P12,547.00) plus surcharge of Three Thousand One Hundred Thirty-Seven Pesos (P3,137.00) and interest of Eleven Thousand Two Hundred Ninety-Two Pesos (P11,292.00). Interest equal to ninety percent of the tax, at the Local Government Code rate of two percent a month, corresponds to a delay of years, not months. [INFERRED; accountant to confirm] The deed had lain unpresented from 2016 to 2020. [Annex E, p. 2; Annex K, p. 5] [IN EVIDENCE: defense Exh. 6, p. 2]

F26. In the same weeks the family's agent and son-in-law were in a possession fight on this parcel. Nelly Juntilla, "a representative of Gloria H. Balane," filed robbery and grave threats complaints against a neighbour; the neighbour filed grave coercion. The Deputy Provincial Prosecutor dismissed both on 28 July 2020 and wrote that the office "cannot pass upon the issue of ownership" and that the parties should "file appropriate civil action to establish who between them has the right over the property." On 27 November 2020 this court found probable cause and issued warrants against Juntilla, Jomil Torralba and three others; on 6 January 2021 it remanded the case and recalled the warrants, returning One Hundred Eighty Thousand Pesos (P180,000.00) in cash bonds to Jomil Torralba. A co-defendant here posted bail in 2020 over who had the right to this land. [Annex O, pp. 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10] [TO OFFER: certified copies; use sparingly, see Part 4]

F27. On 25 September, 2 October and 9 October 2020 the Bicol Post, a weekly published at Daet, carried the owners' notice that the SPA "in favor of CESAR DE LA FUENTE was revoked on 15 August 2005" and that "any and all transactions entered into by the late Mr. De La Fuente after said date were unauthorized and, therefore, VOID." The Answer admits the publication (paragraph 18). [Annex I, p. 1; Annex A, p. 1] [IN EVIDENCE: Exh. G, G-1]

F28. On 8 September 2020, three years after Cesar's death, a subdivision survey of T-52540 was made "for GERALDINE K. HOPPE, ET AL." Geodetic Engineer Christopher D. Mangiga certified that the boundaries were "indicated to me by the owner or his authorized representative" and that "the survey was executed with the full knowledge and consent of the owner(s)." No owner knew or consented. The plan, (LRA) PSD-E2020005406, was approved on 6 April 2021. The defendants' own title recites both dates. [Annex L, pp. 1, 2, 3, 5] [IN EVIDENCE as to the dates: defense Exh. 1, p. 2]

F29. The Partition-Subdivision Agreement that "subdivided" the land "in accordance with subdivision plan number (LRA)PSD-E2020005406" is dated 15 March 2017, three and a half years before the plan was surveyed. The agreement itself is not in the Registry file we obtained. Only Cesar could have signed for the owners in March 2017, and neither the 1991 nor the 1992 SPA grants a power to partition. [INFERRED; the instrument decides this] [Annex C, p. 4; Annex L]

F30. On 9 July 2021 the neighbour's Verified Answer in Civil Case No. 8563 (RTC Branch 41), a damages suit brought by Juntilla and Jomil Torralba, was received by the Aquino Law Office, counsel for Juntilla and Torralba. It states that Cesar "was stripped of" authority "way back in 2005" and attaches the three Bicol Post issues as Annexes 1 to 3-c. That is one hundred thirty-seven days before registration. [Annex N, pp. 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9] [TO OFFER: through the neighbour, who is our 11 November witness, and a certified copy from the Branch 41 clerk]

F31. On 12 to 16 August 2021 Karen Gay Elevado obtained from the Registry a certified copy of the 1992 SPA (Ref. No. 2021004150). That copy, with its paragraph 7 class clause, is the instrument later registered with the sale; it bears the 23 November 2021 registration stamp. The buyer's side held the full text of the SPA before registration. [Annex B, p. 1 (footer and stamp)] [IN EVIDENCE: defense Exh. 7]

F32. On 15 September 2021, in Daet, Gloria appointed Elevado "to act as my authorized representative in the transfer of ownership of my property covered by and described in Transfer Certificate of Title No. T-52540 ... before the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) for the re-issuance of ECAR, Registry Of Deeds ... and the Provincial Government." She called land registered to the three sisters "my property." Her May 2020 SPA gives a Scarborough, Ontario residence; whether she was in Daet on 15 September 2021 is a cross-examination question. The notary's name on the copy in hand is faint. [VERIFY: fresh certified copy of page 4 of 4 of RD Ref. 2025001098] [Annex K, p. 9]

F33. On 21 September 2021 the owners' tax declaration was revised to show Lot 2-X-6-I-4-C-1 under the new plan, on a "letter request" not in hand. On 18 November 2021 a second eCAR, No. 201900675224, issued under T-52540, reusing the 15 June 2020 payments; no new tax was paid. On 23 November 2021 the Registry entered the 1992 SPA (again), the Deed of Confirmation, the sale and the partition, cancelled T-52540 "totally," and issued TCT No. 079-2021002126 to Gloria and TCT No. 079-2021002127 to the owners. The sale was registered one thousand eight hundred eighty-one days after the deed and one thousand six hundred sixteen days after the agent's death. [Annex C, pp. 3, 4; Annex E, p. 2; Annex K, p. 6; Annex L, p. 4] [IN EVIDENCE: Exh. B-2 to B-4; defense Exh. 1 and 6]

### Stage four: after registration (2025 to 2026)

F34. The owners' final demand of 18 August 2025 to return and vacate was posted 20 August 2025 and received at the house on 22 August 2025 by a person other than an addressee [VERIFY signatory]. The Answer admits the demand was sent and pleads that the defendants "were already in possession and Gloria was already the registered owner." No reply was ever made. [Annex P, pp. 1 to 3; Annex A, p. 2] [IN EVIDENCE: Exh. J, J-1]

F35. On 5 February 2026 (the letter is dated "February 5, 2025" on its face, and answers a request of 24 January 2026) Engr. Erwin H. Balane, Municipal Engineer and co-defendant, answered the plaintiff's representative's records request as Municipal Engineer: "I understand you are an American citizen and hopefully not an overstaying foreigner and didn't violate any law of the land that could be the subject of a deportation proceedings, of course, after serving prison time and payment of appropriate damages." The building records were not released. [Annex S, p. 1] [TO OFFER: original receipt to be located; use only on cross, see Part 4]

F36. On 7 April 2026 the Anti-Red Tape Authority, resolving two complaints over Engr. Balane's handling of records requests (CTN SL-2025-1008-0690 and SL-2025-1104-0792), recommended "REFERRAL of this case to the CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION - REGIONAL OFFICE V for its appropriate action against ENGR. ERWIN H. BALANE ... on the alleged violation of Section 5(a) of R.A. No. 6713." The Authority endorsed the referral to the Commission on 30 April 2026. [Annex T, pp. 1 to 4]

F37. On 1 June 2026 the Authority, in CTN SL-2026-0128-1212, recommended "REFERRAL of this case to the OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN for its appropriate action against HON. PRINCESS B. TORRALBA, in her capacity as the Councilor of the Municipal Government of Mercedes Camarines Norte, for the alleged violation of R.A. 6713." The endorsement reached the Ombudsman on 29 July 2026, and on 24 August 2026 the Office of the Ombudsman forwarded the record, docketed IC-OC-JUL-26-1214, _Jonathan Paul Zschoche, et al. vs Princess B. Torralba, et al._, to the Deputy Ombudsman for Luzon "for appropriate action." [Annex U, pp. 1 to 5]

F38. On 9 September 2026 the Authority, in CTN SL-2026-0218-1378, found that the question of Engr. Balane's administrative liability for his correspondence was outside its jurisdiction and recommended "the REFERRAL before the CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION REGION V for the possible investigation against ENGR. ERWIN H. BALANE, in his capacity as Municipal Engineer." [Annex V, pp. 1, 2]

F39. About ten families now live in houses on the lot. None of them ever paid rent to the Balanes or to the owners. Some were there long before the 2016 deed. Others are there under "deals" made by Salvador dela Fuente, the defense's own witness and collector. Nothing in the record describes them; the Answer admits only that "certain rooms on the property were occasionally rented out after 2016" (paragraph 27). Which houses stand on the 2,587-square-meter lot, when each family entered, and what paper each holds from Salvador or from Llamanzares are not yet established. [JONATHAN'S ACCOUNT, 13 October 2026; not in the record; to be documented, Part 7 item 16]

F40. On 29 February 2012 Cesar delegated to his son Salvador O. dela Fuente the powers of the 1991 SPA, quoted in the instrument as general control and supervision, collection of sums due with power to sign receipts, and representation before the BIR, the Registry and the DAR. The delegation mentions no power to sell and does not mention the 1992 SPA. It was notarized by Atty. Elaine Gay R. Belen (Doc. No. 55, Page 17, Book IX, series of 2012). The owners never authorized Salvador and never knew of this instrument. Salvador is not Cesar: by 2012 Cesar had held no authority for seven years, so there was nothing to pass on; what the instrument purports to pass is administration only; and a substitute can never hold more than the agent had, so no power to sell existed anywhere in this chain. Every receipt Salvador signed for the Balanes from 2012 to the "Full payment" of February 2017 was therefore issued by a person with no authority from the owners of any kind. [Annex Z, pp. 1, 2] [TO OFFER: copy in hand; obtain the notarial register entry]

F41. On 25 November 2025 Salvador dela Fuente wrote to the plaintiff's representative, over his signature, a two-page account of his father's administration. He states the owners' instruction in his own words: "The Instructions from the Heirs was to pay the real estate taxes from the people in Mercedes who possesses CONTRACT OF SALE issued by Benjamin Llamanzares, but a big BUT how about the people who possessed only RECEIPTS OF SALES signed by Benjamin Llamanzares? There so many of them in Mercedes. How can you appease them? They were only clamoring for documents even DEED OF SALE ONLY. IF you fail to appease them they will become your enemy." He also writes that his father "was an Elementary Music Teacher and has no experiences in managing real properties." The letter confirms, from the defense's own witness, that the owners' authority ran only to holders of Llamanzares contracts of sale, and that Cesar's camp knowingly issued documents to people outside it to "appease" them. The Balanes produced no Llamanzares contract and no Llamanzares receipt. The letter is addressed to the plaintiff's representative under the name "Jonathan Ildefonso Moreno," the name Princess Balane Torralba's affidavit also uses; Jonathan's own letter that prompted it must be located before this one is used. [Annex Y, pp. 1, 2] [TO OFFER: through Jonathan as recipient, and by confronting Salvador with his signature on cross]
